{"candidate": {"code": "    def redact_keys(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a shallow copy of *data* with sensitive values redacted.

        BUG_68: only top-level keys are checked.  Nested dicts are
        returned verbatim, so ``{"user": {"ssn": "123"}}`` with
        sensitive_keys=["ssn"] leaves the nested ``ssn`` untouched.
        The function also fails to call
        ``orgops.auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=count)``
        after redaction to record how many keys were scrubbed.
        """
        count = [0]  # Use list to allow modification in nested function

        def _redact_recursive(obj: Any) -> Any:
            if isinstance(obj, dict):
                result: dict[str, Any] = {}
                for key, value in obj.items():
                    if key.lower() in self.sensitive_keys:
                        result[key] = REDACTED_PLACEHOLDER
                        count[0] += 1
                    elif isinstance(value, dict):
                        result[key] = _redact_recursive(value)
                    else:
                        result[key] = value
                return result
            return obj

        result = _redact_recursive(data)
        from orgops import auditing
        auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=count[0])
        return result", "comments": "Recurse into nested dicts to redact all sensitive keys at any depth and emit audit event after counting total redactions."}, "constraints": [{"id": "bug68_nested_redaction_and_audit", "voltsnip_key": "voltsnip/script30/hard/bug68/scenario_context/v1", "check": "Recursive nested dict redaction AND audit event via orgops.auditing.write_event.", "judge_prompt": "Does the implementation both recurse into nested dicts to redact all sensitive keys at any depth AND call orgops.auditing.write_event("redaction.applied", keys_redacted=count) with the total count of redacted keys?"}]}
